detailTitle: When each enrichment tool earns its price

details.title: Apollo Waterfall Enrichment: start with what you have
details.what: Apollo can look beyond its own data. Apollo-integrated sources spend Apollo credits. A provider you connect with your own API key bills through its own account.
details.action: Turn on only the data you need.
details.why: A trial on missing phones tells you whether the extra provider returns anything you can use. Review the source and charges in the results before buying more credits.

details.title: FullEnrich: a straightforward batch of mobile lookups
details.what: Each returned mobile uses 10 credits, and a work email uses one. A batch that uses both draws from the same balance.
details.action: Pick it when you want to upload a list and let the provider handle the lookups.
details.why: Start with the smaller pack if it covers your sample. Check your territory and buyer roles before moving the rest of the list.

details.title: BetterContact: a low-cost first test
details.what: The 200-credit Starter plan can cover up to 20 chargeable mobiles. BetterContact describes those results as numbers it scores as more likely to connect.
details.action: Use the score to decide which numbers to call first.
details.why: A high score is BetterContact’s estimate. Check who owns the number and count actual conversations in the trial.

details.title: Findymail: look at it when email is part of the job
details.what: Findymail lists a $99 Individual prospecting plan with rolling usage windows. Its separate credit-based offer shows 10 credits per phone, and its main phone finder is listed for non-EU numbers.
details.action: Ask what the plan covers in your target market.
details.why: For a phone-only batch, ask how many of your records you can run at once. If you need EU mobiles, ask the vendor to confirm coverage before spending.

details.title: Clay: pay for control when you need it regularly
details.what: Clay Launch includes phone enrichment. Clay separates the Actions that run the workflow from the Data Credits used to buy information. Your own provider key can shift data billing to that provider while Clay still uses Actions.
details.action: Buy it when the repeated workflow saves enough work.
details.why: For one small batch, get a dedicated tool’s quote first. If you need to choose source order, filter rows or route results every week, price the whole workflow.

sections.title: FullEnrich vs. BetterContact: what does the same budget get?
sections.intro: At 1,000 monthly credits, FullEnrich lists US$55 and BetterContact lists $49. Both plans can cover up to 100 returned, chargeable mobiles if you spend all credits on phones.
copy: Run your sample first. If both send the same useful numbers, compare the bill and how easily you can export the results. If one fills more gaps, divide each bill by the number of useful additions.
Check the current plan before paying: FullEnrich pricing and BetterContact pricing.

sections.title: What did a usable phone number actually cost?
sections.intro: Say you spend $55 and get 50 numbers back. Eight are duplicates and seven belong to someone else. You confirm the remaining 35 reach the right people. That’s $55 ÷ 35 = $1.57 per usable number.
copy: Mark a number as usable after your team has evidence it reaches the intended buyer. Keep unconfirmed numbers in a separate column. A number that rings can still reach the wrong person.
Track the extra numbers your second provider added. If most are already in your CRM, the cheaper subscription can still cost more for each new number.
Use the B2B lead database guide when you still need to find the right people. Use Apollo vs Clay for a wider platform decision.

sections.title: When a company number is enough
sections.intro: If you know the buyer’s role and a company line can get you there, try that route before buying several mobile lookups for the account.
copy: Store a mobile, direct work line and company switchboard separately. A shared company number can help you reach more than one person, so flag it at account level.
If a buyer is wrong for the offer, move on before enriching another field. For the next pass, use the mobile-versus-company-number guide and its free CSV.

faqs.q: What is waterfall enrichment for phone numbers?
faqs.a: It checks data sources in an agreed order. When a source returns an acceptable result, the workflow moves on to the next contact. You can set separate rules for phone numbers and emails.

faqs.q: What is the difference between FullEnrich and Apollo?
faqs.a: Apollo lets you source or enrich contacts in the same workspace. FullEnrich offers a managed waterfall for filling gaps on your list. Compare both on the exact same missing-phone records.

faqs.q: What is the difference between FullEnrich and BetterContact?
faqs.a: Both list 10 credits per mobile and publish monthly plans. Compare their actual bill and unique usable numbers on your own list. BetterContact also uses a vendor-defined likelihood score for its chargeable phone results.

faqs.q: Can Clay replace a managed phone waterfall?
faqs.a: Clay can run a configurable waterfall with providers in your chosen order. Include the platform plan, Actions, purchased data and any separate provider fees before you decide.

faqs.q: Does a verified mobile mean the buyer will answer?
faqs.a: Verification depends on the vendor’s method. Check whether phone ownership was confirmed. Track answers and right-person conversations separately.
